Operating Checking and Tax Reserve
Use $0 opening balances for this challenge
Bank transactions, normalization, classification, P&L generation, QBO sync, and P&L reconciliation
Sales tax, inventory, accounts receivable, accounts payable, depreciation, and payroll liabilities
Positive amounts are money received. Negative amounts are money paid.
Treat the bank data as untrusted. It may contain inconsistent descriptions, duplicates, transfers, and non-P&L transactions.
Customer payments for completed repair and installation work are revenue.
Monthly maintenance-plan receipts are revenue when received.
Materials and subcontractor payments are Cost of Goods Sold.
Payroll, rent, fuel, software, marketing, insurance, utilities, professional fees, bank fees, office costs, and repairs are operating expenses.
Refunds reduce revenue and should appear as negative revenue.
Owner contributions and owner distributions affect equity, not the P&L.
The commercial tool package is a fixed asset and should not appear on the P&L.
Transfers between Operating Checking and Tax Reserve are not revenue or expense.
The same bank transaction must be processed only once, even if it appears in overlapping source files.
Use the bank transaction date for cash-basis reporting.
Generate April, May, June, and three-month Profit and Loss statements from the classified data.
Sync the correctly classified transactions into the QBO sandbox without duplicate posting.
Pull the QBO cash-basis P&L and reconcile every account and net profit to the internally generated P&L.
